newsitem.title: USA: Tosco buys 500,000 bbls gasoline in NYH.
newsitem.headline: Tosco buys 500,000 bbls gasoline in NYH.

text.p: Tosco Corp was spotted buying 500,000 barrels of gasoline in New York Harbor Wednesday afternoon, according to industry players.
"It's surprising because they're the largest producer of gasoline on the East Coast and they're usually not a net buyer," one trader said.
Tosco owns the giant 290,000 barrel per day (bpd) Bayway refinery in Linden, New Jersey, nicknamed the "gasoline machine" due to the prodigious output of its 135,000 bpd catalytic cracking capacity.

Traders said they suspected a possible problem at the refinery, adding that Tosco had bought this afternoon about 300,000 barrels of conventional unleaded gasoline and 200,000 barrels of reformulated grade for delivery within the next week.
Officials at Tosco's Stamford, Connecticut, headquarters declined to comment, citing routine company policy.
Another trader speculated Tosco might have bought some or all of the barrels to fulfill an exchange agreement with a major refiner.
Under such agreements, refiners supply products to one another as needed, with payment in the form of replacement barrels rather than in cash.
"Bayway has been selling a lot of gasoline in the Gulf Coast," the trader said, with many of the barrels perhaps supplied by the major whom Tosco must now repay in physical barrels.
Tosco purchased Bayway from Exxon in 1993 and the two companies have an exchange agreement to supply each other, traders said.
-- Ransdell Pierson, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1632
